- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after sharp spikes or volatility.
- Overestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, particularly when true values show upward momentum or mean reversion.
- Tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, especially in downward trends — forecasts are too low and take time to catch up.
- Overreacts to recent spikes, overshooting the true value by 2–5% in the immediate aftermath.
- Underestimates mean-reverting periods — fails to recognize when prices are drifting back toward historical averages.
- Shows persistent bias toward lower values in the first 10 days of the forecast, especially when historical mean is high.
- Sensitive to recent low prices — forecasts often dip too low when recent values are near or below 60–65.
